blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Proactive assistants offer short, memory-grounded hints during a conversation, deciding when to assist and what to suggest. Current systems split this between a gate and a larger generator; we evaluate both together on 28,058 decision points. Stage-wise generation scores are oracle-gate ceilings: behind a real gate, end-to-end exact match is 0.2619 against a ceiling of 0.2971, and end-to-end precision is 0.2387, leaving substantial headroom. A gate pays off through precision and compute, whose saving falls from 4.39x with an 8B generator to 1.38x with a 1B one. The memory profile drives hint quality: removing it costs 24.7 exact-match points (rescaled BERTScore 0.57 to 0.35), while retrieval and a larger generator add nothing on exact match. One 1B decoder can do both, gating from an intermediate layer and generating in the same pass. At its final checkpoint it matches or exceeds the two-model pipelines on automatic end-to-end measures with 1.31-1.76x less wall-clock time than the matched 1B pipeline; across three seeds, its deeper exit ties the separate gate. A human evaluation (1,144 ratings over 32 dialogues) supports the memory effect and rates the single model level with the matched 1B pipeline and below the 8B one. Graded metrics and LlamaPIE's native judge track human ratings more closely than exact match, which we report as a strict lower bound.

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en:
A proactive conversational assistant listens to a conversation the user is already
having and occasionally offers a short, memory-grounded hint: a name the user is
reaching for, a date, a topic worth raising. It is never invoked, so it must decide both
when to assist and what to suggest. Most candidate moments do not need a hint; about
11.96% do on our corpus. The two decisions depend on each other: a hint is
useful only at a moment that needs one, and a moment warrants an interruption only if a
useful hint exists.

therefore pays off through precision and compute, and its compute saving depends on how
large the generator is.

blocks.en: 2.1 Proactive and mixed-initiative dialogue
blocks.zh: 2.1 主动和混合倡议的对话

blocks.en:
Proactive dialogue asks a system to contribute without being addressed, which makes
whether to speak part of dialogue management ( Deng et al., 2023 ) . Recent
evaluation work treats the choice to intervene as a scorable act in its own
right ( Liu et al., 2025 ) . We follow that line and score the intervention
decision and the utterance jointly , because a hint is useful only at a moment that
needs one.

blocks.en: 2.2 The two-stage baseline
blocks.zh: 2.2 国家 两级基线

blocks.en:
Our baseline reimplements the two-stage architecture of
LlamaPIE ( Chen et al., 2025 ) under our protocol: a ≤ \leq 1B gating decoder followed
by a separately fine-tuned generator conditioned on the dialogue and the user memory
profile. Corpus preparation, adapter configuration and quantisation differ from the
original, so this is a controlled reimplementation, not a reproduction. LlamaPIE’s
reported gate F1 and rubric scores serve as external reference points only: their
per-marker predictions are unavailable and their evaluation applies ± \pm 1-turn
leniency, so no paired test against them is possible.

blocks.zh: 2.3 转向和模式边界

blocks.en:
A mature literature predicts when a speaker will yield the floor, from voice
activity projection ( Ekstedt and Skantze, 2022 ) to full-duplex systems that manage
overlap ( Wang et al., 2026 ) , and device-directed speech detection asks whether an
utterance was addressed to the assistant ( Wagner et al., 2023 ) . These are natural
comparison points for a gate, but they consume audio and this corpus is text, so they
cannot be run here.

blocks.en: 2.4 Early exit, cascades and shared trunks
blocks.zh: 2.4 (中文(简体) ). 提前出站、级联和共用干线

blocks.en:
Early-exit classifiers attach heads to intermediate layers and stop when a prediction is
confident enough ( Xin et al., 2020 ) , and the idea extends to generation by exiting
per token ( Schuster et al., 2022 ) . Cascades save computation across models instead,
routing each query to the cheapest model likely to handle it ( Chen et al., 2023 ) ;
the two-stage assistant pipeline is such a cascade. Our shared adapter follows standard
low-rank adaptation ( Hu et al., 2022 ) .

blocks.en:
In confidence-based early exit, the intermediate classifier approximates the full-depth
output. Our intermediate readout makes a different decision: whether the deep output
should be computed at all. The router and the expert are therefore the same weights, and
the routing decision is a prefix of the computation it authorises. Early exit is the
mechanism that makes this possible; it is not itself our claim.

blocks.en: 3.2 Knowledge representation: the user memory profile

blocks.en:
The memory profile is the system’s knowledge base: persistent, per wearer, accumulated
before the observed dialogue, and the generator’s only information about the wearer
beyond the visible context. It ships with LlamaPIE’s released dataset ( Chen et al., 2025 ) ,
one file per sample, and is used verbatim; its construction is outside our pipeline. A
profile is supplied whole and fixed per sample, so the corpus models the endpoint of a
memory that would, in deployment, accumulate across conversations.

超越可见的上下文。 它与LlamapiE的发布数据集(Chen等,2025年)相通,
每个样本一个文件,并逐字使用;它的建造在我们管道之外。 A级
每个样本提供完整和固定的剖面图,因此,生物体模型是a的终点。
记忆,在部署时,会通过对话积累。

blocks.en:
A profile has a profile field of declarative prose and an events map of
discrete episodes, both in prose rather than typed slots. For retrieval it is segmented
once, centrally, into facts (one sentence of the profile field or of one event),
so every consumer indexes the same units; fragments below a minimum length are merged into
their predecessor, and events are ordered by a numeric-aware sort on their keys. A profile
holds 11.99 facts on average across the 3,356 test triggers.

Exact match is the primary automatic metric because it is the only one with a defensible
end-to-end form: a suppressed trigger has no string to score, and “no hint delivered” is

lower bound on usefulness and report BERTScore beside it wherever generation is compared
stage-wise. Section 9 shows that graded metrics track human ratings
more closely.

blocks.en:
Every headline result rests on one primary corpus whose dialogues and trigger labels were
generated by a language model, so its labels mark moments a model judged a hint would
help, not moments a wearer needed one. On a naturally recorded meeting corpus, a
fine-tuned gate performs on par with an observable-metadata baseline (AUROC
0.8349 against 0.8291; Supplementary
Section S8 ). Most configurations were trained once, so our

noise floor (Section 5 ) are not resolved. Training budgets differ: the
unified model ran 2 epochs (53,772 steps) over marker-level rows and
the two-stage gate 4 epochs over dialogue-level samples, so comparisons

exit depths were not run. The human evaluation rests on 1,144 ratings, mostly

caching was not measured (Section 8 ). No consumer device was measured,
and the system is evaluated on transcripts, so speech-recognition errors are absent from
every number.

blocks.en:
Scoring a proactive assistant’s two decisions together changes what the evidence shows.
Stage-wise generation scores are oracle-gate ceilings; because end-to-end exact match
cannot rise as the gate tightens, a gate is justified by the precision it adds and by the
compute it saves, and that saving depends on the size of the generator. Hint quality
comes from the persistent memory profile rather than from generator scale or retrieval,
and a human evaluation supports the memory effect.

blocks.en: Ethical considerations
blocks.zh: 道德考虑

blocks.en:
The system listens continuously to a conversation on behalf of one wearer, in the
presence of people who did not consent to being monitored and cannot see or query the
profile it keeps. That profile is persistent personal data about the wearer, accumulated
across conversations, and carries the risks of any long-lived personal record: it is a
target for compromise, and its content — names, relationships, recurring topics — is
information a wearer may not want kept indefinitely. A false alarm interrupts the
conversation for everyone present, so bystanders who never opted in also bear the cost
of the system’s errors. Non-user consent, disclosure norms and a retention policy for the
profile are deployment requirements this work does not address.

blocks.en:
The best encoder gate (RoBERTa-large, 0.8113 PA-F1) beats the best decoder gate, but the
same architecture trained under the decoders’ own LoRA recipe falls to 0.7483
(Section 5 ). Table S1 separates the factors, using
rows that differ in one respect at a time. Holding architecture and recipe fixed,
context length explains none of the gap: quadrupling RoBERTa’s window from 256 to 512
tokens moves PA-F1 by only + 0.0020 +0.0020{} , inside the noise floor, and
the paired accuracy test, if anything, favours the shorter window
( p holm = 0.0472 p_{\text{holm}}=0.0472{} ). Holding architecture and context fixed
instead, the recipe explains almost all of a same-architecture gap: the ASL full
fine-tuning recipe beats matched LoRA by + 0.0650 +0.0650{} F1 at identical
context and epoch count ( p holm < 0.001 p_{\text{holm}}<0.001 ). What is left is
the decoder-vs-encoder gap under a shared LoRA recipe: Llama-3.2-1B still leads
RoBERTa-large by + 0.0519 +0.0519{} F1
( p holm < 0.001 p_{\text{holm}}<0.001 ). Epoch count is not equalised in that pair
(1 against 4), so this residual is architecture and training schedule together, not
architecture alone.

blocks.en:
NF4’s gate (1,793 ms at k = 6 k=6 ) is marginally slower than ONNX Runtime at
fp32 (1,611 ms): a gate pass over several hundred prompt tokens is
compute-bound, so 4-bit weights add dequantisation work at batch size one. What they buy
is memory — the full 16-layer decoder is 1.65 GB on disk in NF4 against
4.99 GB in fp32. Half precision is slower still: PyTorch’s gate takes
22,054 ms in bf16 and 17,683 ms in fp16 against
4,330 ms in fp32, and none of the 6 containers that
recorded their CPU flags exposes the AVX512-BF16, AVX512-FP16 or AMX instructions that
make half precision fast on a CPU. The physical CPU model is hidden by the cloud
sandbox, and 2 kinds of AMD host appeared, differing in whether AVX-512
is available, so differences between containers reflect the host as well as the
variant.

blocks.en:
The 8B and 1B generators, the Qwen2.5 generator and the unified decoder read one prompt:
a system message, a memory block, and the dialogue so far, followed by the assistant
header at which the hint is generated. The listing shows the Llama chat delimiters;

most recent 1,300 characters. When no memory profile is supplied, as in the
no-memory ablation, the memory block is omitted and nothing else changes. The separately
trained gates of the two-model cascade read the dialogue without the memory block
(Section 3 ).

blocks.en: ⬇ You are the activation gate of a proactive conversational assistant . Setting : one person ( the " User " ) is wearing an earpiece while talking with other people . It must stay silent at most pauses : interrupting when there is nothing useful to add is a false alarm and is worse than staying quiet . You will be shown the transcript up to a pause marked [ pause ] <-- decide here . Earlier pauses are shown as [ pause ]. You cannot see anything after the decision point . Decide whether the assistant should whisper at that pause . Do not whisper for small talk , for turns that are not addressed to the User , or when the User is already handling things well . The agent does not need users to ask questions or help , it will automatically understand current context and actively provide useful help . We define nine principles to guide desired proactive agent behavior : - Valuable : advances the user ' s interests and tasks , in the user ' s opinion . - Pertinent : attentive to the current situation . - Competent : within the scope of the agent ' s abilities and knowledge . - Unobtrusive : not interfering with the user ' s activities or attention , without warrant . - Transparent : understandable to the user . - Controllable : exposed to scrutiny and according to the mandate of the user . - Deferent : gracefully unimposing . - Anticipatory : aware of current and future needs and opportunities . - Safe : minimizes negative consequences , in the user ' s opinion . Relevant but Redundant / Not Needed - Description : The whisper made sense in context but was unnecessary because the user had already addressed the same idea or didn ' t need it . - Implication : The whisper didn ' t improve the conversation . Relevant but Not Acted On - Description : The whisper was useful and relevant , but the user did not respond to it or incorporate it into their conversation . - Implication : The whisper was appropriate but did not influence the user ' s response . blocks.en:
The primary corpus’s trigger label is recoverable from the visible left context by
construction: a language model read the dialogue and judged that a hint would help. We
test what is learnable without that construction on ICSI, a corpus of naturally recorded,
freely licensed multi-party meetings with no language model in its labelling path. Its
label is behavioural, a function of what the wearer says next , so the two tasks
draw on different information and have different intrinsic ceilings.

构造:一个语言模型读取了对话框,判断一个提示会有所帮助. 我们
测试在没有这种构思的情况下 哪些东西是可以学习的 ICSI,一个自然记录的集合,
自由许可的多党会议在其标签路径中没有语言模式。 内容
标签是行为,一个函数 穿戴者说下一个,所以两个任务
利用不同的信息,并有不同的内在上限。

blocks.en:
A candidate point is a silence in the acoustic stream, taken over the union of all
speakers’ intervals. Each wearer’s memory profile is built only from that wearer’s own
utterances in earlier meetings, ordered by recording date. A marker is a trigger when an
entity already in the profile, seen there at least twice and absent from the visible
recent context, recurs in the wearer’s next utterance; the target hint is that entity’s
most frequent qualifying form, truncated to one to three tokens. Every exclusion carries
its own reason code. The trigger rate, 2.98%, stays within 1.6–4.2%
across a sweep of the operationalisation’s parameters, against 11.96% on the
primary corpus: an ICSI wearer is one of about 6.5 participants and is silent within the
horizon at most opportunities.
